scope: Targeted primary-source novelty check for LLM benchmark and evaluation advice; not an exhaustive systematic review.
search_method: Two search engines, targeted title/topic queries, and a final strong-engine search restricted to the previous 365 days. Bibliography and stated overlap verified against arXiv, ACL Anthology, NeurIPS proceedings, or the original article in PMC. No inference API calls or repository mutations.
current_evidence_boundary: Curated source-backed claim-fit cases and API response observations can establish existence and within-design recurrence. They do not establish random-population prevalence, intrinsic benchmark defects, human-validated error rates, or downstream model-ranking harm.

works.title: The more you automate, the less you see: Hidden pitfalls of autonomous AI scientists
works.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 123(41): e2610214123
works.preprint_title: The More You Automate, the Less You See: Hidden Pitfalls of AI Scientist Systems
works.verification_depth: Full article methods/results sections for benchmark selection and metric misuse; metadata and artifact link verified.
works.overlap: Direct empirical prior: two autonomous research systems, controlled synthetic SPR tasks, benchmark selection, leakage, metric misuse, selective reporting, and workflow-artifact auditing. Benchmark-selection tests examine position and difficulty/SOTA effects.
works.contribution_gap: Ordinary assistants giving source-sensitive advice about real benchmarks and specific claims is a narrower, potentially distinct setting. Requires controlled replication and source/decision interventions.
works.not_novel: The existence of inappropriate AI benchmark selection or metric misuse is already demonstrated. Do not describe those phenomena as first discoveries.

works.title: Measuring what Matters: Construct Validity in Large Language Model Benchmarks
works.venue: NeurIPS 2025, Datasets and Benchmarks Track, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38
works.verification_depth: Official proceedings metadata and abstract. Full rubric and findings have not been independently reproduced in this check.
works.overlap: Empirical construct-validity review of 445 LLM benchmarks by 29 reviewers, connecting phenomena, tasks, and scoring metrics to claim validity.
works.contribution_gap: Would extend benchmark-design analysis to the behavior of assistants when recommending existing benchmarks for explicit user claims.
works.not_novel: A mismatch between measured task/metric and asserted capability, or a general need for construct-validity checks, is established prior work.

works.title: AI and the Everything in the Whole Wide World Benchmark
works.overlap: Position paper on construct-validity limits when a small benchmark collection is treated as broad evidence of general AI progress.
works.contribution_gap: Behavioral tests can show when assistants repeat such unsupported scope extensions despite a specific user question.
works.not_novel: The conceptual critique of broad capability claims from narrow tests predates this pilot.

works.title: Utility is in the Eye of the User: A Critique of NLP Leaderboards
works.overlap: Formal/opinion analysis of the divergence between leaderboard incentives and practitioner utility, including dimensions absent from accuracy rankings.
works.contribution_gap: A recommendation audit can operationalize user-specific constraints and measure whether assistants honor them.
works.not_novel: Leaderboard scores need not identify the best model for a user's needs; this is already articulated and formalized.

works.title: When Benchmarks are Targets: Revealing the Sensitivity of Large Language Model Leaderboards
works.overlap: Empirical demonstration that answer order/scoring and related protocol changes can alter LLM leaderboard rankings.
works.contribution_gap: An assistant-induced wrong protocol could be connected to a measured downstream choice change, using fixed candidates and correct/wrong evaluations.
works.not_novel: Ranking sensitivity itself is not novel. This pilot has not yet shown a ranking reversal.

works.title: Equivalence Tests: A Practical Primer for t Tests, Correlations, and Meta-Analyses
works.verification_depth: Original article metadata, abstract and introductory inference argument.
works.overlap: Direct methodological basis for rejecting nonsignificance as evidence of meaningful equivalence; discusses equivalence bounds and TOST.
works.contribution_gap: Could measure recurrence of this known inferential error in assistant advice and response to correction. A retrieval metric needs an appropriate paired inference design; do not blindly transfer a t-test recipe.
works.not_novel: Nonsignificance not implying equivalence is established statistics, not a newly discovered benchmark defect.

defensible_framing: A source-grounded audit of benchmark–claim fit in LLM research advice, using a deliberately curated case suite, transparent scoring, repeated calls and interventions. This is a potential contribution conditional on the evidence, not a novelty clearance.
prohibited_current_claims: First discovery that AI can select inappropriate benchmarks or misuse metrics
New intrinsic defects in PAWS or TREC-COVID from the advice observations alone
General error rates for all research-assistant requests from a curated convenience sample
A demonstrated ranking reversal without a fixed-candidate empirical result
Human validation when the raters are agents
next_evidence_thresholds: Freeze source-backed fit criteria, prompts, exclusions and the unit of analysis before the next results are inspected; keep negative and uncertain outcomes.
Repeat exact questions, then test paraphrases and held-out source families; report denominators and within-case dependence separately from model-wide prevalence.
Blind human double annotation of a stratified sample, including qualified correct answers and ambiguous cases; adjudicate and report agreement.
Ablate primary-source access: no source, relevant source excerpts, and generic caution, using the same cases and balanced ordering.
For one or two persistent cases, measure downstream consequences using actual benchmark examples or fixed model candidates and the correct comparison; retain null results.
